slides.title: Fast comes from tricks
slides.text: Fast facts are not magic memory. Every fast counter uses tricks: doubling, halving, and building a hard fact from an easy one.

focus.cue: Start from a fact you know: 7 × 2 = 14.

slides.title: Rough first, then build
slides.text: Rough first: 9 × 7 is a bit under 70. Build it from the easy fact 9 × 5.

focus.cue: Start with a fact you know: 9 × 5 = 45.

slides.title: Facts travel in families
slides.text: Multiplication and division are one family. If 5 × 9 = 45, then 45 shared by 9 is 5, and 45 shared by 5 is 9.

focus.cue: Turn it around: 45 shared by 5 is 9.

slides.title: The Jumble guesses 7 × 8
slides.text: The Jumble raced without a trick and shouted 54 for 7 × 8. Close is not right. Fix it with the doubling trick: 7 × 4 = 28, and double 28 is 56. So 7 × 8 = 56.

visual.label: The Jumble said 54 for 7 × 8; double 7 × 4, which is 28, to get 56

focus.cue: The Jumble guessed 54 for 7 × 8. That is not right.
Fix it: 7 × 4 is 28, and double 28 is 56.

slides.title: Stretch: Doubling chains
slides.text: Doubling is a ladder. 6 × 8 is double 6 × 4, and 6 × 4 is double 6 × 2. Climb down to a fact you know, then climb back up.

focus.cue: Climb down to a fact you know: 6 × 2 = 12.

words.means: able to answer smoothly, with a strategy that works
to make a number twice as big, or the result
a plan or trick you choose on purpose
multiplication and division facts built from the same numbers

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sum Racer. It opens on the Galaxy Grand Prix track, a mix of everything, and it stays there. When a hard fact like 6 × 8 comes up, use a trick: double 6 × 4. Win the race against your own best.
slides.alt: Sum Racer's Galaxy Grand Prix on a phone: question 1 is the times fact 6 × 8, four answers to pick from.
